subject: Temporary SLA carve-out request — preview shard canary (Horizon Analytics)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@horizon-analytics.com>, procurement@horizon-analytics.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary SLA carve-out request — preview shard canary (Horizon Analytics)

Hi Alex / Horizon procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. As discussed, youre planning a limited preview of the new multi-tenant encoding model ("preview-shard-v1") against a subset of your indexing traffic. To support that launch we need a short-lived SLA adjustment so both sides can operate with clear expectations during the canary.

Request (summary):
- Duration: 30 days beginning on the canary start date
- Uptime SLO: 99.5% (vs our standard 99.9% for GA)
- Latency guardrails: median within 1.2x of standard model latency; 95th percentile may increase up to 1.6x during warmups
- Credit policy: pro-rated credits for sustained unavailability beyond the adjusted SLO; details in attached draft

Why this is needed: preview-shard-v1 uses experimental sharding and a new KV cache strategy that materially improves cost for index-heavy workloads but has a small probability of transient latency spikes during cache population and cross-shard coordination. Wed like a brief, instrumented canary so we can validate performance on Horizon's production traffic and tune routing.

Attachments: preview-sla-draft.pdf (draft temporary SLA for review)

Next steps:
1) Please confirm youre comfortable with the 30-day window and proposed SLOs.
2) If agreed, well route a canary with a capped qps and automatic failover to the stable encoder.
3) Ive looped in Marissa (operations) and Grace (customer success) to coordinate monitoring and escalation playbooks. Marissall provide an infra impact assessment.

Looking forward —

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Temporary SLA carve-out request — preview shard canary (Horizon Analytics)

Jordan —

Thanks for the summary. Horizon is willing to run a controlled preview, but we need clearer definitions around the credit policy and the exact failover behavior. A few clarifying questions:

- If the canary triggers automatic failover to the stable encoder, do in-flight requests get retried or failed? We need guarantees for no silent data loss.
- The proposed 99.5% uptime is acceptable for a preview but procurement wants a clause that requires Redwood to notify us and open an incident within 5 minutes of a canary-wide routing failure.
- Can you confirm the max qps were capping the canary at? We dont want discovery traffic to accidentally exceed the canary capacity.

Procurement, please review the attached draft SLA and suggest language for incident notification timing and credit calculation.

If you want, we can push a short MOU to get the canary started while legal finishes the paperwork.

Best,
Alex Turner
Director of Platform Engineering, Horizon Analytics
alex.turner@horizon-analytics.com

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the context. I ran an initial infra impact assessment (attached) and opened JIRA-INF-2981 to track the temporary routing and monitoring changes. Quick summary of constraints and recommended mitigations:

- Routing: canary traffic should be routed to a fixed subset of pods with a hard qps cap. We will implement an immediate circuit-breaker that fails over to the stable encoder; in-flight requests will be retried once by the client-side proxy before returning an error (we will include a retry id header).
- Observability: we will create a dedicated dashboard for the canary (latency P50/P95/P99, error rates, cache hit ratio) and a synthetic probe that will run every 30s.
- Notification & incident: infra will create an automated PagerDuty escalation if the canary error rate exceeds 2% for 3 consecutive minutes; we can also add a 5-minute outbound webhook to Horizons incident endpoint per request.
- Capacity: expected GPU headroom is limited during your global index-run windows (see infra sheet). See infra-impact-assessment.xlsx for numbers.

Open questions for Karthik: can we commit to the 99.5% adjusted SLO for 30 days, and whats the anticipated delta in median latency?

Attachments: infra-impact-assessment.xlsx

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Temporary SLA carve-out request — preview shard canary (Horizon Analytics)

Team —

Confirmed: infra can support a 30-day temporary SLO of 99.5% for the preview-shard-v1 canary under the following conditions:

1) Canary qps cap set to 35% of your normal shard traffic for the first 7 days, then auto-increase to 50% if error/latency targets are met.
2) Automatic failover behavior: in-flight requests will be retried once by the proxy; if retry fails, the request returns an explicit 503 with a retry-id header. No silent drops.
3) Expected latency impact: median +15-25ms (approx +1.1x), p95 up to +120ms (approx +1.5x) during cache warmup; we expect metrics to stabilize after 48-72 hours of steady traffic.
4) We will enable enhanced tracing for the canary and provide a daily canary health digest to Horizon and Redwood CS.

I also recommend the following SLA language tweak for clarity: define a "canary incident" as an event that affects >25% of canary shards for >10 continuous minutes. Credits should be calculated pro-rata on canary traffic subject to that definition.

Ill mark JIRA-INF-2981 as ready for implementation and coordinate a brief runbook handoff. If Horizon signs the MOU, infra can schedule the canary for next-week windows.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime, Redwood Inference
